results.title: A Pragmatic CDO's Field Guide to Data Quality — Part 5
results.content: # **A Pragmatic CDO’s Field Guide to Data Quality — Part 5 — AI That Helps, Not Hypes: ML/GenAI/Agentic Approaches to Data Quality**. ## Where AI earns its keep. We cover label QA and confident learning (Cleanlab), drift detection and robustness (WILDS), feature parity checks, and semantic anomaly detection when rules fail. Agentic runbooks automate lineage walks, owner paging, and contract test generation — always with a human in the loop to keep the system honest. > **Confident Learning for Labels:** Applying confident learning (Cleanlab) to flag label errors and resolve annotator disagreements can significantly boost model performance by cleaning noisy training data [1]. Gold-label audits and active learning loops raise label accuracy, with consensus measured by inter-annotator agreement (e.g. Cohen’s k) [2], [3]. ## Written by Adnan Masood, PhD. Dr. Adnan Masood is an Engineer, Thought Leader, Author, AI/ML PhD, Stanford Scholar, Harvard Alum, Microsoft Regional Director, and STEM Robotics Coach.

As a result, our PD-L1 CPS AI Model, trained in total on over 1.8 million annotations from 533 unique biopsies obtained from 16 labs, detected PD-L1 CPS expression on cell structures with 96.4% agreement against a pathologists' derived consensus score (Fig. 1c).

results.content: **Results:** This preliminary analysis included 34 patients: 24% female, mean age 59 (13) years, median ICU stay 7 [5–13] days, and patients severely ill (APACHE III: 70 (29)). **Introduction:** Real-time body composition assessment is crucial in intensive care unit (ICU) settings for monitoring rapid physiological changes in critically ill patients. For longitudinal data, we used multivariable linear mixed-effects models to find the linear association between the individual metabolite abundance at day 0, 3, and 7 and SF-12 physical component score group 6 months following ICU admission adjusting for age, sex, baseline 25(OH)D, an absolute increase in 25(OH)D at day 3, SAPS II, plasma day, admission diagnosis and patient identification as the random-intercept. **Methods:** Clinical data of 307 consecutive adult patients (47.6% medical, 38.4% surgical) hospitalized in the ICU and selected ECG parameters obtained from standard 12-lead ECG on admission including ST segment deviation (STD), prolonged QTc (prol-QTc) and prolonged QRS duration (prol-QRS) were analyzed.
